target.title: fix(gateway): keep channel lifecycle outside released request admission
target.body:
Closes #110697

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channel accounts started or restarted from a short-lived gateway request could stop accepting later work after that request finished. Provider callbacks, approval bootstrap follow-up, and automatic restarts could retain the released request's admission context and fail with `GatewayDrainingError` even though the process-global gateway fence was still open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel lifecycle work is process-lifetime, not request-lifetime. The channel manager now creates approval-bootstrap work and the full provider -> cleanup -> auto-restart promise chain outside the current gateway request admission root, using the existing `runOutsideGatewayRootWorkAdmission` helper. Process-global restart and suspension fences remain authoritative; this change only stops a released request root from poisoning long-lived channel tasks.

Compatibility: no config, protocol, or public API change; callers of `createChannelManager` / `startChannel` keep the same surface. Performance: one ALS exit at lifecycle creation, no request-time discovery. Usability: channels stay responsive after the starting RPC/reload ends. Security: does not reopen admission during real drain or suspension.

## User Impact

Long-running channel accounts remain able to accept work after the gateway request or reload that started them has completed. Real process restart and suspension still refuse new work normally.

## Evidence

Exact current head: `acb99c7762b982a344065c2e3b71cd9e310d83cc`.

- [Full CI run 29649706201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29649706201): passed, including all four QA Smoke CI profiles.
- Focused production-patch proof on `ca8722dbbc`: `src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` 53/53 passed; `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` 17/17 passed.
- Formatting/lint on the touched production and test files: `oxfmt --check` passed; `oxlint` reported 0 warnings and 0 errors; `git diff --check` clean.
- Added `qa/scenarios/channels/channel-lifecycle-admission.yaml`, an isolated end-to-end QA scenario that starts the real `qa-channel` account through `channels.start`, verifies delivery after that short-lived RPC returns, verifies `gateway.suspend.prepare` rejects an ordinary channel RPC, resumes, and verifies delivery again.

New focused cases:

1. `does not inherit a released request admission into a channel task`
2. `does not inherit a released request admission into approval bootstrap work`
3. `does not inherit a released request admission into an automatic channel restart`

## Real behavior proof

The executable scenario is now in the PR, but its isolated run is not yet claimed as passing.

Attempted from a clean trusted `origin/main` checkout using sanitized AWS Crabbox (`--network public --tailscale=false`, empty instance profile, no hydration). Lease creation failed before PR code was fetched or executed because this workstation has no AWS credentials:

```text
operation error EC2: DescribeInstances, get identity: get credentials:
failed to refresh cached credentials, no EC2 IMDS role found
```

Exact command for an authorized isolated runner at this head:

```bash
OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm openclaw qa suite \
  --provider-mode mock-openai \
  --scenario channel-lifecycle-admission \
  --channel-driver qa-channel
```

Expected observable sequence:

1. `channels.stop` and `channels.start` return for the real QA channel account.
2. After the start RPC root is gone, inbound `QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RPC-OK` produces the exact outbound marker.
3. `gateway.suspend.prepare` reaches `ready`; ordinary `channels.status` is rejected while suspended.
4. `gateway.suspend.resume` returns the gateway to `running`; inbound `QA-CHANNEL-LIFECYCLE-AFTER-RESUME-OK` is delivered.

The focused admission tests and current-head CI are green. The remaining review gap is only the isolated execution transcript for the new end-to-end scenario; this PR does not present the existing unit harness as that transcript.
